pages.title: Schrödinger's Limit
pages.text: The boundary where quantum mechanics stops behaving. It is a still, cold fluid in which superpositions persist indefinitely, never collapsing. Looking at it, I see both outcomes at once. Measurements dipped into it return every answer at once.
$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Pushing quantum systems to their edge, I found a limit beyond which they never collapsed. Schrodinger's cat would live and die forever here.
